result.target_topic: Regulatory capital compliance of specific subsidiaries
result.target_summary: Specific subsidiaries including MSSB, MSIP, MSEHSE Group, MSMS, MSCS, and MSCG operated with capital in excess of their respective regulatory capital requirements as of December 31, 2024 and 2023, complying with requirements from regulators such as the SEC, CFTC, PRA, BaFin, and the Financial Services Agency.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2023 disclosures split the listing of regulated subsidiaries (MSBNA swap dealer status, MSSB, MSIP, MSEHSE, MSMS) into individual paragraphs, while 2024 aggregates them into a single disclosure (D388) listing all such subsidiaries and their respective regulatory capital compliance. D393 (MSBNA swap dealer registration) is thematically linked to the swap dealer registrations listed in D388 (MSIP, MSESE, MSMS, MSCS, MSCG), and the other 2023 disclosures map directly to the entities listed in D388.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2024 disclosures collectively describe the regulatory capital framework: D368 covers the general Basel III/Dodd-Frank framework for the Firm and subsidiaries; D382 covers U.S. Bank Subsidiaries' OCC requirements; D383 covers PCA/well-capitalized status for U.S. Banks; D386 covers MSBNA's specific OCC determination; D388 covers other regulated subsidiaries. The 2025 disclosure ms_2025_8_D378 combines all these elements into a single 'Regulatory Capital Framework' section, covering the Firm, U.S. Bank Subsidiaries, and regulated subsidiaries in one comprehensive overview.

current_disclosures.section: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements > Other Regulated Subsidiaries
current_disclosures.summary: MSCS, the Firm's primary non-bank security-based swap dealer, was divided on February 14, 2026, into Fixed Income and Equities businesses, with the former merged into MSBNA. Additionally, MSESE became a fully licensed credit institution under the EU Capital Requirements Regulation in January 2026, changing its regulatory status.
The Firm is subject to minimum net capital requirements of the SEC and CFTC, and MSCG, a U.S. entity registered as a swap dealer, is subject to CFTC capital requirements.

Certain U.S. and non-U.S. subsidiaries are subject to various securities, commodities, and banking regulations and capital adequacy requirements, and have consistently operated with capital in excess of these local requirements.

comparisons.peer_summary: Failure to meet established capital minimums can lead to mandatory and discretionary regulatory actions with a material adverse impact on the Corporation's financial position; however, the Corporation and its banking entity affiliates were well capitalized at December 31, 2024 and 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and BAC disclose the compliant capital status of their regulated entities. MS states that specific subsidiaries (MSSB, MSIP, etc.) operated with capital in excess of their regulatory requirements. BAC states that the Corporation and its banking entity affiliates were 'well capitalized' at December 31, 2024 and 2023, satisfying established minimums and avoiding the material adverse impacts associated with failure to meet those minimums.

sentences.text: Such subsidiaries include the following, each of which operated with capital in excess of their respective regulatory capital requirements as of December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, as applicable:
Failure to meet the minimum requirements can lead to certain mandatory and discretionary actions by regulators that could have a material adverse impact on the Corporation's financial position.
At December 31, 2024 and 2023, the Corporation and its banking entity affiliates were well capitalized.

comparisons.peer_summary: CGMI and other subsidiaries are registered with the CFTC for futures, swap dealer, and commodity pool activities, and are subject to SEC and CFTC net capital rules that may limit capital-intensive operations and capital transfers to affiliates.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and C disclose that specific broker-dealer subsidiaries are subject to SEC and CFTC net capital rules. MS states that subsidiaries like MSSB and MSIP operated with capital in excess of these regulatory requirements. C similarly notes that CGMI is subject to SEC and CFTC rules specifying uniform minimum net capital requirements, though C emphasizes that compliance with these rules may limit capital-intensive operations and restrict capital transfers to affiliates, whereas MS focuses on the status of exceeding the requirements.

sentences.text: Such subsidiaries include the following, each of which operated with capital in excess of their respective regulatory capital requirements as of December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, as applicable:
• MSSB, a registered U.S. broker-dealer and introducing broker for the futures business, is subject to, respectively, the minimum net capital requirements of the SEC and CFTC.

• MSIP, a London-based broker-dealer subsidiary, is subject to the capital requirements of the Prudential Regulation Authority ("PRA"). MSIP is also conditionally registered with the SEC as a security-based swap dealer and registered with the CFTC as a swap dealer. It currently complies with home-country capital requirements in lieu of SEC and CFTC capital requirements pursuant to applicable substituted compliance rules.
CGMI is also subject to SEC and CFTC rules that specify uniform minimum net capital requirements.

Compliance with these rules could limit those operations of CGMI that require the intensive use of capital and also limits the ability of broker-dealers to transfer large amounts of capital to parent companies and other affiliates.

comparisons.peer_topic: U.S. and International Broker-Dealer Regulatory Oversight
comparisons.peer_summary: Citigroup's primary U.S. broker-dealer, CGMI, and its international affiliates like CGML in London and CGML Japan are subject to specific regulatory regimes including the SEC, FINRA, UK's FCA/PRA, and Japan's FSA.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and C detail the specific regulatory bodies governing their international and domestic broker-dealer subsidiaries. MS lists regulators such as the SEC, CFTC, PRA, BaFin, and the Financial Services Agency for entities like MSIP and MSEHSE Group. C identifies the SEC, FINRA, UK’s FCA/PRA, and Japan’s FSA as the regulators for its primary U.S. broker-dealer CGMI and international affiliates like CGML. Both filings highlight the multi-jurisdictional regulatory oversight of these specific entities.

sentences.text: • MSSB, a registered U.S. broker-dealer and introducing broker for the futures business, is subject to, respectively, the minimum net capital requirements of the SEC and CFTC.

• MSIP, a London-based broker-dealer subsidiary, is subject to the capital requirements of the Prudential Regulation Authority ("PRA"). MSIP is also conditionally registered with the SEC as a security-based swap dealer and registered with the CFTC as a swap dealer. It currently complies with home-country capital requirements in lieu of SEC and CFTC capital requirements pursuant to applicable substituted compliance rules.

• Morgan Stanley Europe Holdings SE Group ("MSEHSE Group"), including MSESE, a Germany-based broker-dealer, is subject to the capital requirements of the European Central Bank, BaFin and the German Central Bank. MSESE is also conditionally registered with the SEC as a security-based swap dealer and registered with the CFTC as a swap dealer. It currently complies with home-country capital requirements in lieu of SEC and CFTC capital requirements pursuant to applicable substituted compliance rules.

Citi conducts securities underwriting, brokerage and dealing activities in the U.S. through Citigroup Global Markets Inc. (CGMI), its primary broker-dealer, and other broker-dealer subsidiaries, which are subject to regulations of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority and certain exchanges.

Citi conducts similar securities activities outside the U.S., subject to local requirements, through various subsidiaries and affiliates, principally Citigroup Global Markets Limited in London (CGML), which is regulated principally by the U.K.
Financial Conduct Authority and Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA), and Citigroup Global Markets Japan Inc. in
Tokyo, which is regulated principally by the Financial Services Agency of Japan.

comparisons.peer_topic: GS Bank USA capital and leverage ratios
comparisons.peer_summary: The filing presents GS Bank USA's leverage ratios, defining average adjusted total assets, the Tier 1 leverage ratio, and the Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR). As of both December 2024 and December 2023, GS Bank USA was in compliance with applicable capital requirements for swap dealers and security-based swap dealers.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS disclose that specific swap dealer subsidiaries were in compliance with applicable capital requirements for those designations. MS states that MSIP and MSEHSE Group (as security-based and swap dealers) complied with home-country requirements in lieu of SEC/CFTC rules or operated with excess capital. GS explicitly states that GS Bank USA, a registered swap dealer and security-based swap dealer, was in compliance with applicable capital requirements for these designations as of December 2024 and 2023.

sentences.text: • MSIP, a London-based broker-dealer subsidiary, is subject to the capital requirements of the Prudential Regulation Authority ("PRA"). MSIP is also conditionally registered with the SEC as a security-based swap dealer and registered with the CFTC as a swap dealer. It currently complies with home-country capital requirements in lieu of SEC and CFTC capital requirements pursuant to applicable substituted compliance rules.

• Morgan Stanley Europe Holdings SE Group ("MSEHSE Group"), including MSESE, a Germany-based broker-dealer, is subject to the capital requirements of the European Central Bank, BaFin and the German Central Bank. MSESE is also conditionally registered with the SEC as a security-based swap dealer and registered with the CFTC as a swap dealer. It currently complies with home-country capital requirements in lieu of SEC and CFTC capital requirements pursuant to applicable substituted compliance rules.
GS Bank USA is a registered swap dealer with the CFTC and a registered security-based swap dealer with the SEC.
As of both December 2024 and December 2023, GS Bank USA was subject to and in compliance with applicable capital requirements for swap dealers and security-based swap dealers.

comparisons.peer_topic: Sources of Restricted Cash and Regulatory Requirements
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm's cash and assets are restricted due to requirements from regulatory authorities, including maintaining reserves at non-US central banks and compliance rules for broker-dealer activities.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and JPM disclose that their broker-dealer activities are subject to specific regulatory restrictions regarding capital and assets. MS notes that its subsidiaries operated with capital in excess of regulatory requirements. JPM states that its broker-dealer activities are subject to restrictions on cash and other assets as part of compliance with respective regulatory requirements, including reserves at non-US central banks. While MS emphasizes the sufficiency of capital, JPM emphasizes the restriction on asset usage due to regulatory rules.

sentences.text: Such subsidiaries include the following, each of which operated with capital in excess of their respective regulatory capital requirements as of December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, as applicable:
• MSSB, a registered U.S. broker-dealer and introducing broker for the futures business, is subject to, respectively, the minimum net capital requirements of the SEC and CFTC.
The Firm is also subject to rules and regulations established by other U.S. and non U.S. regulators.
As part of its compliance with the respective regulatory requirements, the Firm's broker-dealer activities are subject to certain restrictions on cash and other assets.
